stories.headline: Merz pension 'basic cover' remark ignites coalition crisis, prompts 5,000-strong Marburg protest
stories.summary: Chancellor Merz sparked a nationwide controversy when he described the state pension as potentially only 'basic cover' (Basisabsicherung) in a speech to the banking association, drawing fierce backlash from coalition partner SPD, CDU's own social wing, and the public. He spent the week walking back the remark at the CDA conference in Marburg — where 5,000 demonstrators gathered outside — pledging no cuts to statutory pensions while defending a shift toward capital-market-backed supplementary provision.

stories.headline: Pistorius unveils Germany's first-ever Bundeswehr military strategy, targets Europe's strongest conventional army
stories.summary: Defense Minister Pistorius presented the Bundeswehr's first formal military strategy alongside supporting capability documents, setting a target of building Germany into Europe's strongest conventional force with 460,000 troops (active + reserve) by the 2030s, naming Russia as the primary threat. Large sections of the strategy remain classified; critics noted lack of transparency and open questions on funding and conscription timelines.

stories.headline: Germany pre-positions minesweepers in Mediterranean for potential post-war Hormuz mission
stories.summary: Defense Minister Pistorius announced that German naval vessels including minesweeper 'Fulda' would be deployed to the Mediterranean in advance of a potential mine-clearing mission in the Strait of Hormuz after the Iran war ends, citing the need to save time. Pistorius stressed that any active deployment requires a Bundestag mandate and a ceasefire, and named an expansion of the EU Aspides mission mandate as a likely legal basis.

stories.headline: AfD hits record 28% in polling, widening four-point lead over CDU/CSU
stories.summary: A weekly INSA poll for Bild am Sonntag showed the AfD reaching a new record of 28%, leaving CDU/CSU four points behind at 24% and the governing coalition without a parliamentary majority. Multiple polling institutes confirmed the trend. The result intensified pressure on the Merz government and generated analysis of whether mainstream parties are driving voters toward the AfD through reform failures and a perception of political drift.

stories.headline: EU leaders meet in Cyprus on mutual defense clause and post-NATO security architecture amid Trump threats
stories.summary: EU leaders gathered for an informal summit in Cyprus to discuss activating the bloc's Article 42.7 mutual assistance clause amid growing doubts about US commitment to NATO, triggered by Trump's repeated threats over European non-participation in the Iran war. Germany's Merz attended; discussion centered on whether EU defense can complement or partially substitute NATO's Article 5, with Merz and Macron both addressing the framework.

stories.summary: Foreign Minister Wadephul had a diplomatically active week: he blocked a Spanish-led bid at the Luxembourg EU foreign ministers' meeting to suspend the EU-Israel association agreement, calling it 'inappropriate'; visited Dublin to push for ending EU unanimity in foreign policy decisions; and welcomed Hungary's decision to unblock the €90 billion Ukraine credit line following the Orbán government's election loss. He also publicly called on Iran to resume Islamabad talks.

stories.headline: Merz-Klingbeil coalition clash at Villa Borsig summit; reform battles over budget, energy, and taxes deepen
stories.summary: Reports of a heated shouting match between Chancellor Merz and Finance Minister Klingbeil at the April 12 coalition summit in Villa Borsig emerged this week, illustrating deepening coalition tensions over reform priorities. Disputes span income tax reform, an overprofit tax on energy companies (which Klingbeil is pursuing but the EU Commission rejected and CDU opposes), the debt brake, and Klingbeil's participation in a Barcelona summit of left-wing governments.

stories.headline: Klingbeil pushes income tax reform and overprofit tax; EU Commission rejects windfall levy
stories.summary: Finance Minister Klingbeil published plans to cut income taxes primarily for those earning up to €3,000 gross monthly, funded partly by raising the top tax rate and reforming the spousal tax allowance — drawing resistance from CDU/CSU. Separately, his EU-level push for an overprofit tax on energy companies was rejected by the European Commission, leaving the issue to national governments and further inflaming coalition tensions.

stories.headline: Germany summons Russian ambassador over 'direct threats' against targets in Germany
stories.summary: Germany's Foreign Office summoned the Russian ambassador and issued a joint declaration condemning what it called 'direct threats' by Russia against targets in Germany, describing them as an attempt to undermine support for Ukraine and test Western unity. The declaration included a commitment to strengthen air defense cooperation and continue supporting Ukraine's drone industry.

stories.headline: BND marks 70th anniversary as government prepares expanded operational powers via new legislation
stories.summary: Germany's foreign intelligence service BND held its 70th anniversary, during which BND President Martin Jäger called for the service to become Germany's 'first line of defense' with expanded operational capabilities including active sabotage. Chancellor's Office head Thorsten Frei announced a new law would give the BND significantly broader powers, and Merz himself had previously tasked the service to operate 'at the highest level.'

stories.headline: Merz offers Iran conditional sanctions relief in exchange for Hormuz opening and nuclear concessions
stories.summary: Chancellor Merz offered Iran a conditional easing of sanctions at the EU summit in Cyprus, linking the offer to a permanent opening of the Strait of Hormuz, an end to the Iranian nuclear program, and guarantees for Israel's security. The offer came amid EU debate over how to end the Iran war and reflected pressure from rising energy prices.

stories.headline: Reza Pahlavi visits Berlin; German government declines meetings, protester throws red fluid
stories.summary: Exiled Iranian crown prince Reza Pahlavi visited Berlin for political talks with Bundestag members, but was received by neither Chancellor Merz nor Foreign Minister Wadephul, who described him as a 'private person.' A protester threw red fluid at Pahlavi during his visit, and approximately 1,400 demonstrators gathered outside. Iranian exile groups criticized the government's refusal to engage.
